Definition: a mother (as the bond of the family); in a wide sense (both literally and figuratively (like father))
KeyPassages: Genesis 2:24; Exodus 2:8; Leviticus 18:7; Numbers 6:7; Deuteronomy 5:16; Joshua 2:13
BiblicalUsage: In the Old Testament, ʼêm is the word for a mother. In Genesis 2:24, the text says "Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother." In Exodus 2:8, the text says "Go. And the maid went and called the child's mother."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that ʼêm matters because family is God's idea, and the bonds He builds there are meant to hold. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedBooks: Genesis; Exodus; Leviticus; Numbers; Deuteronomy; Joshua
